subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred turn maintenance use an upgrade-safe host-owned bound derived from existing compaction timeout policy, or should OpenClaw permanently expose the new opt-in turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs setting and generic onTaskTimeout queue callback?
rationale: Repository policy sets a high bar for new config and fallback surfaces, the opt-in default leaves the reported user problem unchanged for unconfigured deployments, and the generic queue callback becomes a shared lifecycle contract beyond this one caller.

options.title: Consolidate timeout policy
options.body: Derive an upgrade-safe deferred-maintenance bound from the existing host compaction timeout policy and keep the fencing without adding a second operator knob unless distinct tuning is proven necessary.

options.title: Accept the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the new setting and queue callback as documented permanent APIs, accepting that affected deployments require explicit operator action.

options.title: Split the change
options.body: Land the low-risk stalled-warning backoff separately and pause the timeout/fencing portion until the cancellation contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Consolidate timeout policy
recommendation.body: Derive an upgrade-safe deferred-maintenance bound from the existing host compaction timeout policy and keep the fencing without adding a second operator knob unless distinct tuning is proven necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the permanent compaction and context-engine lifecycle contract assigned to this owner area.
